rows.description: A preschooler says sorry after hurting a friend, often prompted. A forced sorry is only a start, and real apology grows when the child sees the hurt and helps repair it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: A preschooler covers the face or giggles nervously when noticed for a mistake or praise. Embarrassment shows growing awareness of others' views, and kind, private handling helps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, anxiety, embarrassment

rows.description: A young child offers a hug or a toy to a crying friend. Early sympathy is real but simple, and adults can name it so the child learns the link between feelings and care.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, sadness, empathy

rows.description: A preschooler tilts the head, frowns and says huh when something does not fit. Puzzlement is a chance to explain simply and let the child try ideas.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: confusion

rows.description: A young child asks why endlessly about rain, bodies and rules. Questions show thinking, and honest simple answers or a shared search build trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: trust

rows.description: A preschooler jumps up, raises a hand and shouts me first. Eagerness shows motivation, and turn-taking rules help manage the wait.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: excitement

rows.description: A young child crosses fingers or repeats I hope it does not rain for the picnic. Hope is a wish with belief, and honest gentle talk prepares for a letdown.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: hope

rows.description: A preschooler holds up a drawing or a tied shoe and says look. Pride grows with attention to real effort, and shared delight matters more than heavy praise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, pride

rows.description: A preschooler wanders, whines or asks what can I do when nothing holds attention. Boredom is a cue to offer or make choices, and some boredom builds creativity.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: boredom
related concepts: boredom

rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.description: A preschooler's red cheeks may come from embarrassment, heat, running, shyness or pride. Naming the feeling gently helps, while teasing about blushing increases shame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: shame, embarrassment, shyness, pride
